output_json.patch_notes: Root cause: getPrefixLength() classified any path beginning with two separators as a UNC-style prefix, computing prefix length via indexOf(separator, 2)+1 without validating the host-name substring. When that substring was "." or "..", the traversal token was absorbed into the prefix, so doNormalize's dot-dot collapsing loop (starting at prefix+2) never evaluated it, and normalize returned the string unchanged instead of null. Fix: reject the path (return NOT_FOUND) when the host-name substring between the two leading separators and the next separator equals "." or "..". Added regression test testNormalize_rejectsDoubleSeparatorDotDotPrefix covering the PoV payload and bypass variants (backslash, mixed separators, deeper nesting, normalizeNoEndSeparator), plus confirmation that legitimate UNC paths still work.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk, narrow fix. All FilenameUtils/FileSystemUtils tests pass (38/38, 28/28). Full suite has 4 pre-existing unrelated failures from running as root in the container, present before and after this change. Manually confirmed the alert PoV now reports SAFE after patch.
output_json.summary: Fixed CVE-2021-29425-class path traversal in FilenameUtils.getPrefixLength(): a leading double-separator (UNC-style) prefix whose host-name component is "." or ".." is now rejected, so normalize()/normalizeNoEndSeparator() correctly return null for payloads like "//../secret.txt", matching existing behavior for "/../secret.txt". Closes the root-cause defect shared by every trace in the alert.
